demo.cliff: a draft row is a career and an assignment, found by name and never linked
teaches: Linked as the Draft, it answers a refused qualification's Apply to the draft: 1d6 on these six rows, and the row's career is entered at once with no qualification roll, as drafted.

A row names its career in career, by name with case and punctuation folded: the world's Items are searched first, then every Item compendium, and the template found is copied onto the Traveller as a drop would copy it.
careerAssignment fixes the assignment the draft enters on, as rows 1 and 3 do; left blank, as on the other four, the player picks one from the career's own list.
A draft enters past every door the career keeps: the Pilots' Guild on row 5 is entered without its qualification and without the referee's leave.
An event row naming the Draft rolls this table at once and leaves a careerForce on the tray: the drawn career, on the row's assignment, entered as draftedByEvent at the next qualification.
demo.trap: Nothing links this table by itself: unlinked, the draft asks the referee to type a career instead. Only career and careerAssignment are read on a Draft row, and text as the note an event draft leaves; careerMode, the grants and the tray are inert here. A row naming a career that neither the world nor any compendium holds enters nothing: the draft says so and waits for that career to be dropped on the Traveller, who then enters it as drafted. An assignment the career does not carry is not refused either: the player is asked to pick one. Everything but eventTable is inert on a table, and the eleven record fields below it stay empty, as on every template.

system.description: Where the Bellweather levy sends a Traveller the careers turned away: the Reach Guard on two rows, then the harbour, the fens, the Guild and the quay. Invented for this pack, and no book's table.

eventTable.text: The Reach Guard's picket boats are short of hands, and the levy fills them first.
The Reach Guard takes you, and you choose where you serve.
The harbour wants watchmen on its quays more than it wants another gunner in orbit.
A drainage levy sends you out to hold the dykes on the fens.
The Pilots' Guild is short of apprentices for the outer channel, and the levy owes it a crew.
The labour levy puts you to work on the quay cranes.
